Grouped random effects by Laplace-EM on a per-group oracle

Source: R/re_em.R
tulpa_re_em.Rd

The n_quad = 1 sibling of tulpa_re_aghq() on the same per-group oracle: an expectation-conditional-maximisation (ECM) fit of a model whose conditional likelihood factorises over the levels of one grouping factor. Each iteration

  1. solves every group's posterior mode b_g and covariance C_g = Cov(b_g | y) at the current parameters (the E-step, the same per-group solve the AGHQ engine reports as its BLUPs);

  2. updates each random-effect covariance in closed form, Sigma_k = mean_g(b_gk b_gk' + C_gk), projected to its diagonal for an uncorrelated term and floored at sigma_floor^2 on its eigenvalues;

  3. moves the fixed parameters theta (see theta_update).

It stops when the Laplace log-marginal changes by less than tol relative to its size.

Usage

tulpa_re_em(
  theta0,
  re_terms,
  Sigma0,
  make_site = NULL,
  make_group = NULL,
  oracle = NULL,
  n_obs = NULL,
  keep = NULL,
  theta_prior_sd = Inf,
  sigma_floor = 1e-04,
  tol = 1e-08,
  max_iter = 200L,
  theta_iter = 3L,
  n_threads = 1L,
  theta_update = c("marginal", "latent"),
  b0 = NULL,
  newton_max = 30L,
  progress_label = "re-em",
  aghq_debias = 0L
)

Arguments

theta0

Initial fixed-parameter vector. The engine optimizes these jointly with the RE covariance; the callback interprets them.

re_terms

A list of RE term specs (or one spec), each defining a covariance block: n_coefs (block dimension \(c_m\)), optional correlated (default TRUE for c_m > 1; FALSE gives a diagonal block), and n_groups (shared across terms). For the make_site path each term also carries idx (1-based group index, length n_obs) and, for a slope block, Z (the n_obs x n_coefs design). For the make_group path the per-observation idx / Z are optional – the callback owns them – and the term needs only n_coefs / correlated / n_groups.

Sigma0

List of initial per-term covariance matrices (the EM estimate).

make_site

function(theta) for the single-arm separable case, returning a list with: eta_re (length n_obs, the RE-arm fixed predictor), deriv = function(rows, eta) returning list(logL, d1, d2) (per-row marginal log-likelihood and its first/second derivatives w.r.t. the RE-arm predictor eta, used for the per-group mode), and lmat = function(rows, ETA) returning a length(rows) x ncol(ETA) matrix of per-observation log-likelihoods over the quadrature node columns. Supply this or make_group, not both.

make_group

As in tulpa_re_aghq(); the list it returns may also carry joint(g, b), returning list(logL, grad, negH, theta_grad, theta_info, cross): the grad_hess blocks plus the data theta score \(\partial \ell_g / \partial\theta\), the theta observed information \(-\partial^2 \ell_g / \partial\theta^2\) (n_theta x n_theta) and the cross block \(-\partial^2 \ell_g / \partial\theta \partial b\) (n_theta x d). theta_update = "latent" requires it.

oracle

Optional prebuilt native (compiled) oracle, an external pointer to a REGroupOracle (constructed in a consumer package's src/ via LinkingTo: tulpa against <tulpa/aghq_oracle.h>). When supplied the engine drives it directly, with no per-group / per-node round trip into R, and neither make_site nor make_group is needed; re_terms, theta0 and Sigma0 must still describe the same layout the oracle exposes. The integration core is identical to the R-closure path.

n_obs

Number of observations (length of each term's idx). Required for the make_site path; ignored for make_group.

keep

Optional logical/integer mask of observations to include (default all; make_site path only). Rows outside keep are dropped from every group.

theta_prior_sd

Prior standard deviation of theta, one value or one per coordinate; Inf leaves a coordinate unpenalized.

sigma_floor

Floor on every random-effect standard deviation, applied to the eigenvalues of each covariance update.

tol

Relative tolerance on the change in the Laplace log-marginal.

max_iter

Maximum EM iterations.

theta_iter

Maximum BFGS steps on theta per EM iteration.

n_threads

Threads for the per-group loops, used only when the oracle declares itself thread-safe. The result does not depend on it.

theta_update

"marginal" (default) or "latent"; see Details.

b0

Optional n_groups x d matrix of starting group modes (d the total random-effect dimension, terms in re_terms order). Absent, the latent rule starts every group at zero and the marginal rule at each group's own solve.

newton_max

Maximum joint Newton steps per iteration (theta_update = "latent").

progress_label

Label of the progress line and heartbeat (the tulpa.nl_progress option sets whether they are written).

aghq_debias

Latent rule only: a per-axis node count > 1 adds one adaptive Gauss-Hermite moment step at the converged mode. Each group's posterior second moment is integrated on the AGHQ engine's tensor grid (centred at the mode, scaled by the group's posterior covariance) and the covariance update takes their mean, which removes the Laplace small-cluster attenuation of the variance components; the group covariances and the theta covariance are then recomputed at the new covariance through the likelihood curvature. 0 (default) skips it.

Value

A list with theta, theta_cov, theta_hessian (the theta curvature theta_cov inverts; theta_cov is NULL when it is not positive definite), theta_se, Sigma_list, log_marginal (Laplace), blup, blup_var, blup_cov_g (per-group posterior covariances), blup_cross_g (mode/theta cross-Hessian blocks, the Bf of tulpa_re_aghq()), group_ok, converged, n_iter, blup_cross_available, log_marginal_trace, stuck (latent rule: the final joint Newton accepted no step at any damping, so converged is FALSE), aghq_debiased (whether the aghq_debias step ran; it leaves the Laplace fit in place when a factorization or quadrature sum fails); NULL with a warning when the per-group solve fails at the start.

Details

theta_update = "marginal" moves theta by BFGS on the Laplace marginal at the current covariance, with its exact (envelope) gradient, and reports the inverse curvature of that marginal as the theta covariance. Its gradient differentiates each group's Hessian in theta, which the engine does by central differences.

theta_update = "latent" treats theta as a latent Gaussian variable with prior N(0, theta_prior_sd^2), as INLA treats fixed effects: theta and every group's mode are solved jointly by a damped Newton on the penalized joint log-density (the Hessian is an arrowhead, solved through the Schur complement of the random-effect blocks), and the theta covariance is the inverse of that Schur complement. It needs only first and second derivatives of the group log-likelihood, including its theta score: a native oracle supplies it, and a make_group callback through its optional joint closure (below). With a Gaussian conditional and theta entering the linear predictor, the two rules reach the same theta.

See also

tulpa_re_aghq() for adaptive Gauss-Hermite marginal fit on the same oracle.
